summary: Minakshi Banerjee works in Indology. Banerjee completed doctoral studies under Debarchana Sarkar and held the James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society, both attested in 2026.
Mineo Hashimoto (1924–1984) worked in philosophy and religious studies. Hashimoto studied at Kyoto University and held a post at Kobe University.

Ming Mei works in Buddhist studies. Mei earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Qingli Wan, and studied at SOAS University of London under Roderick Whitfield, Tao Wang, Shane McCausland, and Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu earned a BA from the University of Hong Kong and a PhD from UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Robert Epp, later serving as professor at Hong Kong.
Mingyu Fu works in Buddhist studies. Fu earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi, attested in 2013.

Minori Nishimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata, Seiren Matsunami, and Kenyo Mitomo. Nishimura held posts at Taisho University, Sanko Cultural Institute, and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Harvard, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts and a professorship at the University of Tokyo, and served as President of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo. From circa 1963 to 1993, Kiyota served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg (Dr. phil.). Warren held posts at Johns Hopkins University, the American Academy in Rome, and Harvard University.
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipam Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo between circa 1860 and 1899.
Miranda Shaw is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Shaw studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Bucharest and studied at Calcutta; his career included posts at Bucharest, Sorbonne University, EPHE, and a professorship at the University of Chicago.
Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Helffer held a post at the CNRS from circa 1961 to 1993 and was affiliated with Paris Nanterre University in 1985.

Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. Lingorska has held posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich, both attested in 2026.

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker. Albahari held posts at Western Australia and UNSW.

Miriam Levering is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She received her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee.

Mirjan Damaška studied at Zagreb, the Hague Academy, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Ljubljana (PhD). Damaška held academic posts at Zagreb, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale Law School.
